quotes.text: The default maximum, without increased large-charge limits, is 999,999.99. If Stripe enables increased limits, the absolute hard cap is 9,999,999.99 for two-decimal currencies. Merchant or platform Risk limits can lower the effective maximum.
When a customer files a dispute with their bank, Stripe sends you the [charge.dispute.created](https://docs.stripe.com/api/events/types.md#event_types-charge.dispute.created)
When the dispute closes, Stripe sends you the [charge.dispute.closed](https://docs.stripe.com/api/events/types.md#event_types-charge.dispute.closed) webhook event.
Stripe can automatically retry each failed PAD payment once, no more than 30 days after the original payment attempt.
The customer completed the Checkout Session. The payment outcome isn’t final yet.

old_evidence.text: It can take up to 5 business days after initiating a payment to receive notification of success or failure. PADs aren’t a guaranteed payment method.

When a dispute is created, Stripe sends both the [charge.dispute.created](https://docs.stripe.com/api/events/types.md#event_types-charge.dispute.created) and [charge.dispute.closed](https://docs.stripe.com/api/events/types.md#event_types-charge.dispute.closed)
By default, Stripe automatically sends emails to the customer for these cases.
With Direct Debit retries, Stripe can automatically retry failed Direct Debit payments caused by insufficient funds.

findings: The November capture greatly expands the same ACSS/PAD URL: new account eligibility and provisional review (24–38), 0.50 minimum and conditional maximum tiers (44–46), explicit capture/refund/dispute capability matrix (54–78), refund lifecycle (79–105), event-specific dispute flow (107–129), Connect capability and mandate rules (248–256), retry limits (258–264), asynchronous completion events (278–313), and mandate-ID lookup (315–340). The older capture already establishes Canadian customers, CA/US businesses, mandate and verification, T+4/T+5 timing, and delayed/non-guaranteed payment (old 8–76, 111–129). These are dated guide statements, not verified eligibility or live account configuration.

Current source line 42 and wiki/concepts/stripe-acss-debit.md:51 say charge.dispute.created and charge.dispute.closed are simultaneous. Old raw 194 said both were sent when a dispute was created, without independently proving simultaneous delivery; new raw 119 says created is sent when the customer files and closed when the dispute closes. Remove simultaneous timing, preserve the bank-final/no-counter-evidence rule (new 123–127) and personal 90-calendar-day versus business 10-business-day windows (old 192; new 113).

Source line 37 and concept lines 40–45 call the required recurring notice a pre-debit notice before each charge. The captures instead say notify on each debit and use charge.pending as the custom debit-notification trigger (old 170–188; new 181–198). Keep the mandate confirmation deadline of five calendar days and all-or-nothing custom-notification obligation, including applicable microdeposit reminders; avoid an unsupported blanket before-each-charge deadline or confusing the pending event with final debit success.

The new guide distinguishes submitted/processing state from final outcome: Checkout's checkout.session.completed is session completion only (new 309), while checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded/failed and payment_intent.succeeded/payment_failed indicate delayed payment results (new 302–311). A payment can fail after initiated or even rarely after PaymentIntent succeeded, at which point Stripe records a failure-reason dispute and fee (old 200–216; new 131–135). T+4 payment success and T+5 funds available are after submission, not creation, and neither establishes customer-bank receipt (old 111–121; new 266–276).

New line 46 specifies limits conditional on Stripe enabling increased large-charge limits and potentially lower merchant/platform Risk caps; do not treat 9,999,999.99 as the default. New 250–256 requires PAD capability on both platform and connected account and a new mandate for each connected merchant of record when on_behalf_of is used; the old source only notes descriptor ownership and old raw 267 prohibits reuse of another connected account's mandate. New 338 gives the PAD mandate-ID path in the account owning the PaymentIntent; it does not expose an ACSS network transaction ID.

New 260–264 narrows automatic Direct Debit retries to failed PAD payments caused by insufficient funds: at most one retry within 30 days, no debit failure fee for Stripe-initiated automatic retries. Old raw heading 269 labeled Billing Retries private preview; the new heading omits that label but does not establish general availability. Similarly, the new product table's off-session ✗ at 224 must be read with its product/integration context, not used to erase old interval-mandate or subscription use. Checkout subscription mode remains unsupported (old 92; new 227, 240).
substantive_changes: Add the new dated raw reference and summarize conditional transaction limits, asynchronous status events, Connect capability/per-connected-account mandates, retry bounds, and refund/dispute lifecycle. Correct the source and concept's simultaneous-dispute-event assertion using new raw 119.

Qualify source/concept debit-notification timing against the old and new charge.pending trigger and each-debit language; retain mandate-confirmation and microdeposit email obligations without asserting a universal pre-charge deadline. Preserve the old private-preview label as historical, without inferring a release status from the new omission.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain old raw/stripe-acss-debit-2025.md as historical evidence for CA/US business versus CA customer scope, CAD/USD currency mismatch risks, mandatory mandate and verification, delayed confirmation, and separate T+4 success/T+5 Stripe-balance availability.
Retain the old capture's private-preview Billing Retries heading (old 269) as dated wording; the new guide supplies retry limits without a release-phase assertion.

Preserve mandate schedules (interval, sporadic with express at-payment consent, combined), personal/business transaction type, mandate cancellation's effect on future debits, and default_for invoice/subscription setup. Separate merchant of record and Stripe-account ownership for Connect mandates and descriptors.
conflicts: wiki/sources/source-stripe-acss-debit.md:42 and wiki/concepts/stripe-acss-debit.md:51 assert simultaneous dispute.created/dispute.closed; new raw 119 explicitly places them at filing versus closure. Old raw 194's combined sentence did not prove simultaneous delivery.

wiki/sources/source-stripe-acss-debit.md:37 and wiki/concepts/stripe-acss-debit.md:41/45 assert a pre-debit notice before every charge; old raw 170–188 and new raw 181–198 say notification each time a debit is made and custom notification triggered by charge.pending, without a universal before-charge timing claim.

The current source's line 52 private-preview Billing Retries label is the old raw's dated label (old 269); the new guide's line 258 heading lacks a phase qualifier. Do not silently convert that omission into GA or assert the older phase is verified current.
unresolved_questions: The new capture's instant provisional access, account review, large-charge limit enablement, connected-account capability and custom Radar preview do not establish any particular merchant's live eligibility or configured limit.
The new guide omits a Billing Retries release-phase label, so whether its old private-preview status changed is unresolved by these two captures.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/acss-debit, the November capture adds explicit conditional transaction limits (new 44–46), refund/dispute lifecycle (new 79–129), Connect mandate prerequisites (new 248–256), retry bounds (new 258–264), and delayed-outcome events (new 302–311). The older guide already established mandatory mandate/verification and up-to-five-business-day non-guaranteed confirmation (old 8–16), plus T+4 payment success versus T+5 Stripe-balance availability (old 111–121). [[source-stripe-acss-debit]] should add these dated facts and avoid treating checkout.session.completed or a pending debit as final payment success.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/acss-debit, [[source-stripe-acss-debit]] and its ACSS concept need a material correction: their simultaneous dispute-event claim overreads old line 194, while new line 119 sends charge.dispute.created on filing and charge.dispute.closed at closure. Their pre-debit-before-each-charge wording should follow the raw's each-debit notification and charge.pending trigger (old 170–188; new 181–198). Preserve the 180-day refund window, bank-final PAD dispute, and old private-preview retry label as historical; the new retry detail at 260–264 does not establish general availability or a successful payment for a specific merchant.
